secondary_audiences: Loudoun-area Indian-American families (B2C — pantry-restock, daily cooking)
Loudoun-area home cooks across communities curious about Indian cooking (B2C — entry SKUs, recipes-on-the-shelf)

tagline: Whole spices, fresh ground. Two Loudoun locations.
short_intro: We grind cardamom, cumin, and coriander in the back of the shop — never more than two days old. Two stores: Ashburn and Herndon, open every day.

featured_products.name: Idukki green cardamom (whole)
featured_products.why_signature: Bangalore market grade, not export — the pods you'd pick yourself if you walked the market

featured_products.name: Hand-ground sambar masala
featured_products.why_signature: Ground fresh every Tuesday at the back of the shop, 18 spices, the smell of Tuesday afternoon

featured_products.name: Basmati rice 1121 (long grain)
featured_products.why_signature: Aged 18 months, 8mm-plus grain — the rice that doesn't break when you make biryani

competitive_lens: Edge against Patel Brothers / House of Spice is the freshness signal (ground in-store every Tuesday, named-origin SKUs like Idukki cardamom + Basmati 1121). Edge against generic grocers is the depth of catalog + the Indian-American owner who knows what 'sambar masala that smells like home' means.
